We are entering the final few weeks of a pilot project which is likely to cause very high QuotaGuard usage for another two or three weeks and then drop down to much lower levels.  The use case we have is an endpoint which uses IP-based authentication which we need to hit from our systems, which use an IaaS provider that does not currently support static outbound IPs.

Would it be possible to explore customised pricing options for the rest of our project? 

Best wishes
Nick White

Hi Tim,

I was about to do this change when I noticed the configuration is not the same between staging and production apps.
Is there a way to load different config files depending on env? What’s the risk of push the same config file (with all configurations) to all apps?

Best,
Saulo
On Mar 2, 2021, 7:16 PM -0800, QuotaGuard <tim@quotaguard.com>, wrote:
Hello,

We wanted to bring a potential issue to your attention.  You are using the QGTunnel software in your applications and they are still set to download the tunnel configuration from our dashboard.  This can be handy during initial setup of the QGTunnel, but now may pose a startup risk to your application.

In the last 24 hours your 16 applications downloaded the configuration from our servers over 2000 times.

Our dashboard can be down from time to time for regular maintenance.  During this time if one of your applications attempts to startup QGTunnel, it will fail to run because it cannot find the configuration on our servers.

This problem can be avoided by downloading your QGTunnel configuration as a .qgtunnel file.  When this file is placed in the root of your project, QGTunnel will find the configuration locally and not attempt to download it from our dashboard.  This will harden your setup by removing a dependency.

You can download your configuration file by signing into our dashboard from heroku and then going to Setup, QGTunnel Configuration, and then clicking the Download button at the top right.

If you need further assistance in this effort, please reach out to support@quotaguard.com or simply reply to this email.

Tim
QuotaGuard Support

subject: [BUG][URGENT] bin/qgtunnel is overriding env variable
description:
Hi,

We recently experienced memory issues in our production environment. Backtracking, it seems like it is due to jemalloc being disabled. And it seems like the `bin/qgtunnel` script (retrieved as stated here) is the problem.

Indeed, `strings bin/qgtunnel | grep LD_` indicates that is it set within the script. Moreover, I’ve used a simple script `bin/foo`:

#!/usr/bin/env bash

echo "buildpack=foo preload='$LD_PRELOAD' at=start-app cmd=$@"
$@


Which I used in our `Procfile` to check for LD_PRELOAD changes (e.g: `bin/foo bin/qgtunnel bin/foo REDACTED`). And here’s the result:

2021-03-31T09:59:40.887290+00:00 app[web.1]: buildpack=foo preload='/app/vendor/jemalloc/lib/libjemalloc.so ' at=start-app cmd='bin/qgtunnel bin/foo REDACTED'
2021-03-31T09:59:40.907783+00:00 app[web.1]: buildpack=foo preload='/app/vendor/nss_wrapper/libnss_wrapper.so' at=start-app cmd='REDACTED'

Could you fix that by not overriding but rather do the usual pattern, that is done for instance by the jemalloc buildpack:

export LD_PRELOAD="/app/vendor/jemalloc/lib/libjemalloc.so $LD_PRELOAD"

Best,
Ulysse

subject: My account has been suspended
description:
Hi guys,

I can see that my account has been suspended for exceeding the bandwidth limit. What i'm confused about is that my heroku instance was switched off, so i'm not sure what is running up my bandwidth usage (I've only just now enabled it). I've reviewed the QG logs and some requests are hitting around the 1mb mark. I guess i'm trying to wrap my head around why these requests are so expensive in terms of data usage, is there anything unusual that you can spot with my setup?

I don't know how i've managed to spend my data allowance. If it's perhaps a leak on my app somewhere in terms of hidden/chaining of requests I can fix that, but i've engineered my app to sparingly execute API requests to my Mongo clusters with a range of caching strategies.

Any pointers would be appreciated!

Thank you

Kind regards
Farhan

subject: Socks proxy for connecting to PostgreSQL with a static IP
description:
Hi there, 

Do you have any guides/documentation for connecting to postgres databases with a socks proxy? 

I have a number of Heroku apps (NodeJS), which I need to connect to another organisation's PostgreSQL RDS database on AWS (through a static IP). The DB is sitting within a VPC, however they have created a publicly accessible reader node and are whitelisting our IPs. 

I have tried using the Heroku Fixie-Socks add-on, however the example they provide uses a socks library that hasn't been updated in 6 years (`socksjs`), and relies  a very old version of the `pg` library. 

Ideally, we'd like to switch to QuotaGuard, but I haven't been able to find any examples of how to use this to achieve what we need.



Thanks for your help, 

Christopher

subject: pg_restore from Heroku to Azure
description:
Hello,

I'm trying to use QuotaGuard but I think I'm stuck.

What I want to achieve:
I have an app deployed to Heroku with the Postgresql database as an add-on. This is the app's primary database.

There's another Postgresql database in Azure.

I want to run a worker in Rails to simply pg_dump database on Heroku and pg_restore it in Azure.

I've whitelisted QG's IPs in Azure's firewall. I've created a tunnel with following config:

[qgtunnel.0]
accept = "127.0.0.1:5433"
connect = "AZURE_DATABASE_HOST:5432"
encrypted = false
transparent = true

I'm just using DATABASE_HOST as an example. In my config, it's the string name of my remote database.

I've changed my Procfile and with the debug mode I can see:

Starting process with command `bin/qgtunnel bundle exec puma -C config/puma.rb`
Created proxy dialer for http://rjnc5tazvpd1t5:t4jdxdi8ippzex6wys1i6hv6wk4qj4@eu-west-static-01.quotaguard.com:9293
Found tunnel configuration {"Tunnels":{"0":{"accept":"127.0.0.1:5433","connect":"AZURE_DATABASE_HOST:5432","transparent":true,"encrypted":false}}}
Added DNS override for AZURE_DATABASE_HOST:5432
Starting listener on 127.0.0.1:5433 for AZURE_DATABASE_HOST:5432
Finished initialization
Starting new process /app/bin/bundle with args: [bundle exec puma -C config/puma.rb]
Starting dynamic tunnel monitor
Started process. Waiting for it to exit

After that, I connected to Heroku's bash, created a backup with pg_dump, and wanted to restore it to Azure's database.

I tried with:
pg_restore --verbose --clean --no-acl --no-owner -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U AZURE_USER -d AZURE_DATABASE -W latest.dump

but it resulted in a connection error
Is the server running on host "127.0.0.1" and accepting
TCP/IP connections on port 5433?

same with

pg_restore --verbose --clean --no-acl --no-owner -h AZURE_DATABASE_HOST -p 5433 -U AZURE_USER -d AZURE_DATABASE -W latest.dump

and same with

pg_restore --verbose --clean --no-acl --no-owner -h AZURE_DATABASE_HOST -p 5432 -U AZURE_USER -d AZURE_DATABASE -W latest.dump

Am I missing something? I've whitelisted my local IP and can connect and restore to Azure's database without a problem, just not on Heroku.

Amazon Web Services

---- On Tue, 16 Feb 2021 13:00:07 +1300 Tim Day <staticsupport@quotaguard.com> wrote ----

Hi Lucas,

If you aren't using transparent mode, then your application will work without it.  You can either add the missing .so file (directions below) or you can turn off transparent mode in your configuration.

Transparent mode allows us to override the DNS setting for your destination hostname to be localhost, which is where the qgtunnel is listening.

To add the missing .so file, redownload qgtunnel into the root of your project:
 curl https://s3.amazonaws.com/quotaguard/qgtunnel-latest.tar.gz | tar xz  

Commit and push your code:
Be sure that  vendor/nss_wrapper/libnss_wrapper.so  is also added to your repository.  Git skips .so files by default, you will likely have to add it with:
 git add -f vendor/nss_wrapper/libnss_wrapper.so 

Tim

subject: Guidance on Quotaguard IP restriction service.
description:
Dear Support Team,
We have a usecase, where we want to whitelist 2 of our IPs and provide to an external 3rd party service.

We want to setup Quotaguard to provide us with these 2 IPs.

We noticed you have 2 of such services:
1. QuotaGuard Static IP
2. QuotaGuard Shield Static IP

We have the following questions.
1. We need guidance on which one to use - Quotaguard Static IP or QuotaGuar Shield Static IP.
2. We also want to know if there will be any side effects when setting up this service, like downtime due to loss of connectivity with some of our existing users who connect to our API services?
3. How soon can we set this up?
4. If we decide to stop using the service are there any side effects like downtime due to loss of network connection because of changing IP address, etc?

Thanks, in anticipation of your swift response.


Sincerely,

Theo Kamma

Any response will be much appreciated!

Thanks,
Yuriy

subject: Quota Guard tunnels / SSL Connection / Attempts for unauthorised access
description:
Dear all,
We are experiencing severe attempts for unauthorized access to our database. We use Quota Guard tunnels for connecting to mongo. However, the automatic encryption offered by Quota Guard is not working, probably because we use our own certificate for the encryption between Heroku and the domain provider. Unfortunately, this allows third parties to see through the tunnels and to try getting direct access to our database.
Therefore, we will appreciate it if you can provide us documentation that describes how to encrypt the connection to the database ASAP! Can you offer us your own certificate or should we use the same certificate already used for the encryption between Heroku and the domain?
Thank you!
Kind regards,

subject: Connecting to External Postgres From Heroku
description:
Hi,

My goal of signing up to QuotaGuard was because I want to implement IP based limiting of connections to my Postgres Database hosted in DigitalOcean.

My application reveknew on Heroku is a Java SpringBoot application which connects to the Postgres database via JDBC. When I limit access to the database to  the 2 IP addresses in my QuotaGuard account  the application is no longer able to connect to the database.

This presupposes that there’s some additional work I need to do to enable my application initiate connections to the database as if connecting from 1 of those 2 IP addresses. 

Can you enlighten me on the way forward to achieve this? 

Otherwise I perhaps have misunderstood the benefit of QuotaGuard to me and might as well no longer use it.

Todd

Hi,
First of all, welcome to QuotaGuard Static, we're happy you've decided to try out our service. This email should get you up and running in no time.
Please keep this email for future reference, as it can help with setting up, reaching out to support, knowing your configurations, and answering general FAQ.

Accessing Static IP Connection Settings

You can start using our service immediately using the credentials we added to your dyno in the QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_URL environment variable.
Additionally, your Static IP connection information can be found in your QuotaGuard administrator dashboard.
To reach the dashboard, either run $ heroku addons:open quotaguardstatic or click on the upper right arrow next to the QuotaGuard Add­on. If you have trouble finding it, please follow Step 6 from the instructions in this blog post, How to Provision the QuotaGuard Add-on.

Your Static IPs

  • 54.72.12.1
  • 54.72.77.249
Please allow all IP addresses for any whitelisting or firewall rules, as traffic may route through any of the IP addresses at any time.

Subscription Information

Username: quotaguard8274
Proxy Password: Located in your dashboard

Connection Strings

HTTP url: http://quotaguard8274:{PASSWORD}@eu-west-1-babbage.quotaguard.com:9293 (for HTTP and HTTPS traffic)
SOCKS url: socks5://quotaguard8274:{PASSWORD}@eu-west-1-babbage.quotaguard.com:1080 (for all types of TCP traffic)

Testing Your Connection

via Heroku CLI

$ heroku run 'curl -x http://quotaguard8274:{PASSWORD}@eu-west-1-babbage.quotaguard.com:9293 -L ip.quotaguard.com'

via Curl

$ curl -x http://quotaguard8274:{PASSWORD}@eu-west-1-babbage.quotaguard.com:9293 -L ip.quotaguard.com

Inbound Proxy

If you are looking to use the inbound proxy, you will need to upgrade to the Micro plan or higher. To upgrade you either run $ heroku addons:upgrade quotaguardstatic:micro or change the plan from the Resource tab on the heroku dashboard.
Setup instructions for Inbound Proxy's and Custom Domains can be found at Getting Started with QuotaGuard's Static IP Inbound Proxy.

Support

To access support and get help, we have a few options for you, or you can just open a new ticket at our Support portal and we will answer you directly.
  • Heroku Documentation for QuotaGuard Static.
  • Setup Support for configuring with Node.js, Ruby, Python, Go, Java, and PHP, etc.
  • Setup QuotaGuard for MongoDB
  • Check out our FAQ.
  • Need to Create a Support Ticket?
  • News and Announcements? Find them at our Blog
  • Request for Dedicated Proxy Setup (Enterprise plans and higher)
  • Do you have Privacy, GDPR, or Legal Questions?
Thanks for giving us a try and don't be shy about reaching out for help, we're always here to assist with any questions you might have.
Michael
QuotaGuard Static
P.S. If you are working with sensitive data like HIPAA, Financial, or Personally Identifiable Information (PII), you will want to check out QuotaGuard Shield. It's the same as QuotaGuard Static but with stronger end to end security for your requests.

subject: Shield with socks5 proxy, seems not to work as expected?
description:
Hi, I'm having some trouble getting Shield to work as a socks5 proxy.  It just seems to not respond with any data.

As a test, I'm using the curl commands.  Curl can apparently be used to test socks proxy behavior too.  So for our Static instance, these both work (with the correct username and password substituted, of course):

curl -x 'http://USER:PASS@us-east-static-01.quotaguard.com:9293' ip.quotaguard.com
curl -x 'socks5://USER:PASS@us-east-static-01.quotaguard.com:1080' ip.quotaguard.com

But for our shield instance, only the first one works

curl -x 'http://USER:PASS@us-east-shield-01.quotaguard.com:9293' ip.quotaguard.com
curl -x 'socks5://USER:PASS@us-east-shield-01.quotaguard.com:1080' ip.quotaguard.com

Note that I'm guessing here that the port for socks with Shield is the same as for Static.  (I also tried 1081 to check if it followed the convention of being 1 higher)  The config page for the Shield proxy doesn't list anything about socks, which is surprising.  The pricing page and docs all state that Shield should work with socks.

Thanks for any help you can provide!
Aaron

  b. Link to supplier's information security policy
  c. Other relevant policies

Thank you very much and appreciate your time responding to our queries as we gear up to expand our usage of QuotaGuard's services.

subject: mongodb+srv with QGTunnel?
description:
Hi, I'm trying to run a Heroku application that points to MongoDB Atlas. They use the "mongodb+srv" protocol on their connection strings. I have added tunnels for the base URL as well as all three of the individual servers in the cluster, but am still getting "connection refused" from Atlas.

If I disable the IP Whitelist on Atlas, it connects successfully, so there is definitely a QuotaGuard configuration issue.

I did notice that the mongodb+srv protocol does not allow a port to be specified. QuotaGuard requires a port, so I've set it to 27017...maybe this is the problem? But I don't know what to set it to...

How do I support this?

    <?php

    try{
        $result = curl_exec($ch);
        curl_close($ch);
    } 
    catch(Error $e) {
        $trace = $e->getTrace();
        echo $e->getMessage().' in '.$e->getFile().' on line '.$e->getLine().' called from '.$trace[0]['file'].' on line '.$trace[0]['line'];
    }

    }

Here's my Node.js router code:
    const express = require("express");

    router.get("/", (req, res) => {
      Data.find()

    router.post("/", (req, res) => {

Can anyone help me resolve this?

Perhaps Michael you can better explain to me what I can do in this situation.

Thank you in advance

subject: QuotaGuard Shield SOCKS5 dropping connections
description:
Hi Tim,

I wanted to follow up on the SOCKS5 connection issue that you have been troubleshooting for the past few weeks. 

To summarize, we first started testing QuotaGuard Static IP on our Heroku app about a month ago and pretty soon ran into issues with the SOCKS5 proxy intermittently dropping connections. We reported this and had provided you access to our test app to help troubleshoot the issue.In the meantime, we tested QuotaGuard Static Shield and that proved to provide a more stable SOCKS5 proxy, so after testing it out in staging we deployed it to production on our first app. Yesterday we deployed it to our second app and after a few hours of deployment ran into the same issues with the proxy dropping connections. This caused a considerable amount of production downtime for us and we have disabled the add-on for now.

Have you been able to find the root cause of the connection issues? We had planned to expand the add-on to other apps if it had worked, but it looks like we will have to stop using it because it seems to be fairly unstable.

Thanks,
Rishi

subject: How Does QuotaGuard Handle Session Cookies?
description:
Dear QuotaGuard Tech Support:

We are embarking on using your platform for communicating with a system that uses session cookies for accessing their API.

The basic flow is as follows:
1. Invoke their “login” endpoint with pre-defined credentials. This returns a cookie value.
2. Invoke their “getCookieName” endpoint. This identifies the cookie’s name.
3. Thereafter, our system can invoke their APIs without re-authenticating by virtue of the presence of the HTTP session cookie.


The vendor platform that we’re connecting keeps that cookie valid until we invoke their “logout” endpoint, so it’s definitely long-lived.

I noticed that your proxy is keeping the cookie. Can you tell me the lifetime and how that cookie is managed by the QuotaGuard proxy?

Kind regards,

Nick
--
Nick Jacobs | Senior Tech Lead
nick@yoco.com

- Node.js, using Feathers.js framework
- Connect with Knex.js
- Deployment with Docker container to Heroku
- PM2 as a process manager

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

John Young

description:
Hi!

I'm trying to setup QuotaGuard on Heroku project.

1. I added QGStatic addon.

> heroku run 'curl -x http://otatuwfjt4dtk8:*****@us-east-static-07.quotaguard.com:9293 ip.quotaguard.com'
{"ip":"54.84.66.109"}
It works

5. Added qgtunnel to application `bin/` folder.
> curl https://s3.amazonaws.com/quotaguard/qgtunnel-latest.tar.gz | tar xz

6. Setup Procfile:
web: bin/qgtunnel npm start
Can see that it is running on startup (heroku logs)
That command is using PM2 to start nodejs application

I'm using address 127.0.0.1:27017 to connect to Mongo, so by theory it should go through the tunnel. But it doesn't. :(
Don't see even unsuccessful requests in QG logs.

Please help!
What did I forget to do to make it work?

subject: Intermittent SSL Expiration Issue and SSL Update
description:
Hello,

We currently use your service to provide static IPs to our clients for network whitelisting.

We use your service through the Heroku add-on ecosystem. Our app names in Heroku are ‘remip-prod’ and ‘remip’

For remip-prod we’re forewarding to https://remip-prod.herokuapp.com utilizing the following domains: 380e99ab8b87ac02-us-east-1.getstatica.com and remip.archmrt.com

When we first set up the service, we used a star cert that covered *.archmrt.com

Since then for security reasons, we wanted to disable the TLS 1.0 protocol. On Heroku, to do this, you must stop using their automated certificate management SSL setup that most people in their common runtime use. To disable TLS 1.0, you must provision an SSL add-on and upload your certs directly to the add-on.

Because we we’re wanting to do this for both our staging and production environments, we ended up having to provision two separate certificates specifically for the subdomains that we use (remip.archmrt.com for production and remipstaging.archmrt.com for our staging environment).

We updated both with separate SSL endpoints and separate certs for the subdomains.

What we were unsure of is if we needed to update the SSL certificates for our in-bound proxy setups on your service. We are getting users reporting intermittently getting a SSL expired error when interacting with our production environment. Our staging environment looks to be fine.

To cover our bases, we wanted to reach out to you and get some input on what should be our next steps. Do we need to upload our subdomain specific certs now as part of the in-bound proxy we have setup with QuotaGuard Static? Any help would be appreciated. I guess part of our confusion is that since we used the same star cert for both our production and staging instances, if there was an expiry issue, why wouldn’t we be seeing the same SSL cert errors in our staging environment as we are in production.

Also of note, the epired certificate issue is only happening for particular users. One user who is seeing it is using a slightly older version of Google Chrome (version 81.0.4044.138 (Official Build) (64-bit). We have users with up to date versions of Chrome who are not seeing the issue. We are looking into if it’s a matter of updating the browser, but we wanted to connect with you on this as well to see if you’ve encountered any problems with a particular browser.

Thanks,

Philip Carlson
Consultant for Arch Capital Services

subject: Questions about your Heroku add-on offerings.
description:
Hi there! We've been exploring your product and had some questions we were hoping you could answer.

We are a campsite/glamping listing platform, and our hosts often sync calendars between us and other sites like Airbnb. Other sites have per-ip rate limits which we work within. We poll their calendars at regular intervals to keep our information up to date. Although this polling sometimes hits rate limits, it's not a big deal for us.

We want to introduce real-time calendar syncing while users are completing bookings on our platform, to ensure there are no conflicts. This service cannot afford to hit rate limits, so we were thinking of using dedicated IPs to perform these checks.

At the moment, we do not need static IP addresses.

My understanding is that Quotaguard Dynamic IPs is the appropriate product for this. I wanted to confirm how this product works. My question is essentially - what are the guarantees around not hitting rate limiting? 

I also noticed there is Quotaguard Static IPs. Are the two IP addresses we are provided with, exclusive to us? If not, how does this guarantee rate limiting will not occur?

Thank you for your time and I appreciate your patience as we learn about your product!

Best regards,

-Myles

Thanks,
Greg Meyers

​

Hi michael, now I finally understood why I had all these requests, because it seemed really strange to me that in April we had made 99 requests while in just 4 days of May there were already 168!.... Sorry again for the trouble I caused you and have a nice day!
 
Matia Fazio

Thanks,
Prabha

subject: Understanding Heroku add on plan
description:
Hi,

My name is Joaquín, I am sending this email because I have issues understanding this Heroku add-on completely. I am currently developing a web application that, among other things, is scraping another web application. In order for my application to scrape the other one I am using proxies. In particular I am paying for a plan in Stormproxies. I am currently facing the issue to upload my application to Heroku only to find out that Heroku doesn't provide you application with an static IP address so that I cannot white list it on the Stormproxies service unless I change my server provider (Heroku), integrate it with an add-on that gives you an static IP or change Stormproxies with an add-on that replace it. Searching for the third solution I have found you. Sorry for the long introduction but I need you to answer me a couple of questions if you can, and thinking from my perspective.

1- Do you know if your clients use this service for scraping? and if is it good for the purpose?
2- How often is the IP changed, in between requests? every 3,or 5 minutes?
3- In your plans I can only see requests limits for Daily goolgle maps requests and for freegeoip.net requests, what is the limit for another web site? (for the scraping purpose)
4- Only the Enterprise plan gives HTTPS API support, does that mean that the other plans doesn't give you the proxies service of redirecting you  when you are hitting an https request?

Thank you in advance for helping me, I hope my writing is not that bad.

Regards,

Joaquín Ricci

Michael

description:
Hi,

I am trying to connect to MongoDb Atlas through QuotaGuard using this guide : https://support.quotaguard.com/support/solutions/articles/12000066411-how-to-connect-to-mongodb-using-quotaguard

What I have so far:

I am running a Node.js REST server inside a Docker image.  My Dockerfile looks like this :

FROM node:10-alpine

WORKDIR /app

COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm install -g

COPY . .

CMD [ "bin/qgtunnel", "npm", "start" ]

[qgtunnel.0]
accept = "127.0.0.1:27017"

encrypted = false
transparent = false

My process starts successfully and I get no error logs but I can't connect to Mongo DB. I also don't seem to be getting any requests coming to quoataguard.

Any ideas?

Thanks,
Stephen

subject: Migrate to a Dedicated Resource for your Account
description:
Hey everyone,

  I hope everyone is doing well and excited about the upcoming weekend. 

  We have a small request, your production app (bbhotel-digital-prod) is currently on a shared proxy, and the resources on that shared proxy are starting to get used up as your shared customer base on that proxy continue to grow and use more resources. It will likely start to see some residual effects over the short term (slower processing of requests, latency, etc) that we don't want you to experience as a Premium customer. 

  Before that starts to happen, we'd like to move your app to a dedicated resource where you won't be susceptible to those issues like you currently are on the shared proxy. Obviously, dedicated resources give you more security, flexibility, and scalability than a shared resource.

  The process for this move would be, once you green light the plan, we would build your dedicated proxy in the background and send you the new credentials. This new proxy obviously would have a different set of IP's and a different connection URL for passing requests through. Once we've built it, you can then test the new dedicated proxy out, make sure you can connect and route traffic successfully, before choosing a time to make the change.

  At a time convenient for you, you can make the hot swap change to the new proxy. We can also be on standby in case anything doesn't appear successful, however we've never had one of these fail to work on the first try. Also, one can always switch right back to the shared resource if there are any issues. Both proxies would be available throughout the process, just in case. 
 
  Would this change be something we can fit into your near term schedule? I hate to bump this into your normal course of business, but long term we believe it's going to present a much better customer experience for HotelBB.com. 

  Just reply to this email with questions, thoughts, and a green light to get building behind the scenes for you. 

Michael

subject: Heroku + Quotaguard Shield + AWS RDS MySQL
description:
Hello!

My company is interested in using Qutoaguard Shield to proxy our AWS RDS MySQL connections from our heroku servers in order to whitelist communications.
It's mission critical for us to maintain encryption throughout the entire line of communication.
We use Node for our servers. Our following code doesn't seem to establish a connection with our MySQL servers due to some incorrect SSL configuration. Can you please let us know if we're doing something wrong (see code below)? We're trying to force SSL throughout the entire line of communication. We are passing the AWS CA in mysql_server_options to establish a sock connection to the remote database. Our database has force_ssl enabled.

Thanks so much!
Best,
Marc

const url = require('url');
const SocksConnection = require('socksjs');

// SOCKS Proxy for fixed IP
const proxy = url.parse(QUOTA_GUARD_URL);
const auth = proxy.auth;
const username = auth.split(':')[0];
const pass = auth.split(':')[1];

const socks_options = {
host: proxy.hostname,
port: 1080,
user: username,
pass,
};

const mysql_server_options = {
host: process.env.DB_MYSQL_HOST,
port: process.env.DB_MYSQL_PORT,
user: process.env.DB_MYSQL_USER,
password: process.env.DB_MYSQL_PASSWORD,
database: process.env.DB_MYSQL_DB,
ssl: {
ca,
},
};

module.exports = () => {
return new SocksConnection(mysql_server_options, socks_options);
};

description:
Hello,

My company is interested in using QuotaGuard Static for a Ruby on Rails application in Heroku. We will probably need the Deluxe or Super plan for our production Heroku application. We need it to provide a fixed IP address for our applications connection our MySQL database.

My question: Is there any way to use your product easily without our staging server Heroku apps needing the Quotaguard-addon installed, only in production? It will be too expensive for us to use it on every staging server since we have over 10, and only want this to be a production solution. However, I could not get the setup to work on Heroku applications that don't have Quotaguard installed and the tunnel setup.

To further complicate things, we are using AWS RDS which does not have a fixed IP itself. Please let me know your advice, I was thinking of possibly using Socat.

Best,
Alec Dibble

subject: Error in the PHP Example for QuotaGuard Shield
description:
Hi,

I tried using QuotaGuard Shield in my Heroku PHP application but could not get it working with the following code snippet from your documentation (https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/quotaguardshield#https-proxy-with-php):

<?php

function lookup() {
$quotaguard_env = getenv("QUOTAGUARDSHIELD_URL");
$quotaguard = parse_url($quotaguard_env);

$proxyUrl = $quotaguard['host'].":".$quotaguard['port'];
$proxyAuth = $quotaguard['user'].":".$quotaguard['pass'];

$url = "https://ip.quotaguard.com/";

$ch = curl_init();
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_URL, $url);
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_PROXY, $proxyUrl);
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_PROXYAUTH, CURLAUTH_BASIC);
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD, $proxyAuth);
$response = curl_exec($ch);
return $response;
}

$res = lookup();
print_r($res);

?>

It results in a 504 Gateway Timeout error, and nothing get logged into the dashboard. After some searching, the problem seems to be that the cURL option CURLOPT_PROXYTYPE is set by default to CURLPROXY_HTTP, but it should be set to CURLPROXY_HTTPS, because QuotaGuard Shield uses a HTTPS (not HTTP) proxy. The same code snippet probably works fine in QuotaGuard Static, because it uses a HTTP (not HTTPS) proxy.

In other words, you have to add the following line into the code snippet: curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_PROXYTYPE, CURLPROXY_HTTPS);

After that, everything seems to work fine.

In order to avoid other potential users from running into the same problem, I would strongly recommend updating the code snippet as soon as possible. Could you also confirm that it is otherwise valid and up-to-date for QuotaGuard Shield and that no other changes are required in comparison to QuotaGuard Static?

Best regards,

subject: Heroku multi-app setup
description:
Hi QuotaGuard team, 

Thanks for the awesome job that you've done on this add on. 
As a user currently using quota guard in production, I'd like to know how I can make my existing setup working with your system in a multi-app deployment scheme. 

Let me explain. 

I've got application A, which is using a quotaguard enterprise account for a few years now. Everything is OK, but I'd like to add another app, B, and benefit from the static IP addresses of A. 

According to your setup, and, as I am on heroku, I've done the following: 
- setup QUOTAGUARD_STATIC env variable linked to application A 
- installed NSS wrapper, to use transparent mode 
- launched my app with qgtunnel 

But, unfortunately, this is not sufficient to benefit from the tunnel entries of my application A in my application B. When I resolve a distant URL which should be transparently proxied with the DNS resolver, it doe give me the final destination, and, all of my requests never reach my proxy. 

Could you have a look? 

Thanks a lot

 Have a great rest of your week,
 
Michael

Hello,

We're using transparent mode to implement quotaguardstatic socks5 proxy with qgtunnel.
In the deployment step it says "If you are using transparent mode, be sure vendor/nss_wrapper/libnss_wrapper.so is also committed.". Where is this file located? Is it part of the bin/qgtunnel file in the root file? If so how would I check? I am unable to open tunnel because it is a binary.

Thanks,
Orlandson Asturiano

subject: Dropped Http Requests
description:
Hello,

I'm writing because we are receiving errors occasionally when POST'ing over Quotaguard to one of our partners. Our logs appear to drop the connection somewhere while our partner claims they receive the request successfully and respond with a 200.

We are using Ruby 2.6.3 with Faraday Gem and when the error occurs we receive a generic Connection Failure with "EOFError"; basically the connection fails after about a second.

This is an issue because we being charged by our partner but receive an error.

Is there any way to see logs of HotelEngine's request through Quotaguard? Is this something that is likely to happen with Quotaguard? We use the same method of requesting over HTTP with other partners and only seem to have this issue using Quataguard.

Please let me know if there is anything I can do to help.

subject: Bandwidth Limit Issues
description:
Hello,
 
I’m a developer that’s part of our data integrations team at ThinkLP. I’m reaching out to get a better understanding of how the bandwidth limits work, to see if it’s related to an issue we are currently having.
 
Username: w4ib7xizu00r7i
Product: QuotaGuard Static
 
Summary
 
We are currently using the QuotaGuard Static product as an add-on for one of our Heroku apps. We are currently on the Spike plan, which provides 5000 static IP requests per month. Where we believe we are having issues, is related to the bandwidth limit, which is 250MB.
 
We’ve been noticing that when we connect to an external FTP server using this service, we will consistently get timeouts, or prematurely closed connections when attempting to download a file larger than a certain size, usually north of 100MB. Also, it consistently fails around the 10 minute mark.
 
When we don’t use the static IP, we don’t get those issues at all, so the assumption is that there must be a hard limit somewhere that’s causing this issue, whether it’s bandwidth or timeout related. How does the bandwidth limit work? Is it per IP request? Per day? Per month? If it’s possible to verify any of these assumptions and/or provide some insight into this, that would be of great help
 
Thank you,
 
Dannie Wynter
ThinkLP – Loss Prevention & Safety Management Software

                  ​
                    Which QuotaGuard should I use?
                  ​
                    We offer three products on Heroku, QuotaGuard, QuotaGuard Static, and QuotaGuard Shield.
                  ​
                    QuotaGuard routes your traffic through a dynamic set of IP addresses that may change at any time and is intended for accessing APIs like Google Maps that restrict usage based on your IP address. It should be used if you want to access these APIs without your limit being shared with other Heroku apps.
                  ​
                    QuotaGuard Static routes your traffic through a pair of static IP addresses that never change. It should be used if you need your traffic to pass through a known IP address for the purpose of firewall ingress rules or application whitelisting with a third party. QuotaGuard Shield uses HTTPS for outbound service and SSL Passthrough for inbound service. Shield allows you to utilize Heroku’s ACM for your site or bring your own certificate without having to upload it to our servers.

subject: Questions about QuotaGuard plans on Heroku
description:
Dear QuotaGuard representative,

At EduMe we have a need to offer a whitelisted IP range for one of our clients (they are a teleoperator and want to zero-rate traffic to our API from a mobile app, so static IP for inbound requests is the use case).

We run our API on Heroku and QuotaGuard looks like a suitable packaged solution to achieve this. As we are considering QuotaGuard Static / Shield for this, a few questions came up:

1) At what point of our development and deployment cycle could we provide the static IP addresses to our client? Is it possible to get/reserve IPs in advance, or if not, can we sign up for a free plan, inspect the IP addresses, and retain the same IP addresses when we upgrade to a plan that suits our production needs? (so far we're thinking we'd need Enterprise or Premium, but upon closer inspection we may find out that a different level is appropriate or sufficient).

2) Is it possible to use QuotaGuard Shield on Heroku to transparently handle a subset of requests sent to a particular API App on Heroku (I assume we would need to point two different domain names to this App, one through QuotaGuard Shield and one directly to Heroku - I don't think configuring the right client apps to use these would be a problem for our particular use case).

3) Have I understood correctly that two key differences between QuotaGuard Shield and QuotaGuard Static are that the former is more demonstrably secure and has the added benefit that SSL certificate management would not change from our existing setup in any way?

Best regards,

Mikko Heikelä
CTO, EduMe
